title: Default type parameters and inference
hook: Default type parameters let callers omit generic args when the default fits — Promise<void> defaults resolve type, and ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'> relies on defaults deep in React types.

blocks.text: Syntax: `interface ApiResponse<TData = unknown, TError = string>`. If caller writes `ApiResponse<User>`, `TData` is `User` and `TError` defaults to `string`. Defaults apply **right to left** when partially specifying type args: `Foo<A, B = BDefault, C = CDefault>` — `Foo<X>` sets A=X, B and C use defaults. **Inference** from value arguments can still override defaults. Defaults appear throughout lib.d.ts — `Array<T>`, `Promise<T = void>` in some patterns, and custom hooks.

entries.plainDefinition: Fallback type when caller omits that type argument.
Supplying only leading type args — rest use defaults.
entries.example: Map<string> // invalid — must supply all or infer

entries.plainDefinition: Inferred types beat defaults when arguments provide evidence.
entries.example: createState(0) infers number over default unknown

entries.plainDefinition: Parameters without defaults must come before those with defaults.
entries.example: <T, U = string> valid; <T = string, U> invalid

blocks.text: Library APIs use defaults to reduce boilerplate — `EventEmitter<T = any>` (legacy), modern libs prefer `unknown`. React `useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)` needs explicit type because default null inference differs. C# has `class Foo<T> where T : new()` but default type args are `class Foo<T = string>`. Senior interviews ask when inference fails with empty arrays and how defaults fix `useState<number[]>([])`.

blocks.title: Defaults vs inference
blocks.body: Defaults apply when type arg omitted — inference from values is separate and usually wins when present.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Pick sensible defaults
items.body: unknown over any for safety; void for no-return generics.

items.title: Order parameters
items.body: Required type params first; defaulted ones trailing.

items.title: Combine with constraints
items.body: T extends Entity = DefaultEntity — default must satisfy constraint.

items.title: Document when to omit
items.body: Most callers use defaults; power users override.

snippet.label: Interface with defaulted error type
snippet.explanation: Line 1: E defaults to Error. Line 5: only T specified — E is Error. Line 6: override E to string.

snippet.label: Function default fixes empty array
snippet.explanation: Line 1: default T = string when no arg clues. Line 5: empty call gets string[]. Line 6: explicit number[] override.

snippet.label: Multiple defaults right-to-left
snippet.code:
type CacheConfig<
  TKey extends string = string,
  TValue = unknown,
  TTL extends number = 3600
> = { key: TKey; value: TValue; ttl: TTL };

type DefaultCache = CacheConfig; // all defaults
type UserCache = CacheConfig<'user', User>;
snippet.explanation: Line 7: no args — all defaults apply. Line 8: partial — TTL still defaults to 3600.

snippet.label: Failure mode — default any hides bugs
snippet.explanation: Default any makes store.get() return any — poisons chain. unknown forces narrowing.

blocks.title: Default any
blocks.body: T = any in public APIs — prefer unknown or a concrete default.

blocks.title: Wrong parameter order
blocks.body: Required type param after defaulted one — syntax error.

blocks.text: Conditional types can use defaults: `type Foo<T = never> = ...`. React 18+ types chain defaults across ComponentProps. When inference and defaults conflict, explicit type args win. `NoInfer<T>` (TS 5.4+) blocks inference from specific positions — defaults apply instead. Library design: minimize type params; default the least important ones trailing.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot explain partial type arg specification. Default any in API design. Confusing inference with defaults.

interviewTakeaways: T = Default in angle brackets — used when type arg omitted.
Required type params before defaulted ones.
Inference from values often overrides need for explicit args.
60s: Defaults reduce boilerplate in generic APIs. T=unknown safer than any. Partial specification fills trailing defaults. useState/array cases need explicit or default.
Follow-up: NoInfer, conditional type defaults, React prop defaults.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "defaults are runtime values" — compile-time only.
Strong: "Default type params when arg omitted. Order matters. Prefer unknown. Combine with constraints."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS default function params are runtime; TS default type params are compile-time only.
C# and TS share T=Default syntax — both apply at compile time; C# also reifies generic args at runtime.
